result.title: E-MAPS: Event-Based Promptable Video Segmentation with Memory-as-Prompt
result.summary: RGB-based video object segmentation (VOS) remains brittle under fast motion and adverse illumination. Event cameras preserve signal under blur and challenging exposure, but provide little evidence when motion slows. Interaction can restore object state for subsequent propagation, yet promptable event methods merely address single windows. We formalize event-based Promptable Video Segmentation (ePVS), where prompts at arbitrary windows initialize, correct, or introduce objects and predictions. We present Event Memory-As-Prompt Segmentation (E-MAPS), which transfers a pretrained promptable segmenter to event streams and learns propagation and correction. Event-to-Token (E2T) aligns recurrent event features with pretrained representations while preserving prompt-conditioning priors. Memory-Aware Prompting (MAP) converts object-conditioned history into sparse prompts, allowing memory and user inputs to share one decoder pathway efficiently. We construct Event-View Masklets (EViM) from 206K aligned RGB-event pairs and 620K masks for two-stage representation transfer and native event-video learning, and establish three training-disjoint benchmarks. E-MAPS leads prompt-once and interactive ePVS across all three benchmarks while being more efficient. It further demonstrates strong performance on zero-shot object tracking benchmarks. Project page: https://github.com/adonaydem/emaps-wacv

AI.brief_summary: 提出基于事件相机的可提示视频分割任务 ePVS 与 E-MAPS：把预训练可提示分割器迁移到事件流，用 Event-to-Token 对齐循环事件特征，并以 Memory-Aware Prompting 将对象历史压缩为稀疏 prompt，与用户输入共用一条解码路径，同时构建 EViM 数据与三个基准。
AI.relevance_reason: 「把历史记忆转成稀疏 prompt 并与交互输入共享解码通路」可能为 LVR 中 latent 记忆与视觉证据如何注入推理状态、以及输入退化时证据筛选提供可供核查的接口设计，但其任务是分割传播而非多模态推理。
